correctness.rationale: Fix a center for the full trace. A different center on one arm covers only that arm among the neighbors; a center at distance two can cover at most two neighbors on distinct arms; farther centers cover none. These facts rule out shattering four: if the original center is a support point, it cannot be dropped while retaining a mixed-arm triple of neighbors; otherwise a mixed-arm triple forces the original center and thereby the fourth point. Collinear triples fail the two-positive trace. The remaining triples have distance patterns (1,1,2), (2,2,2), (1,2,2), and unique full-trace centers. Offsets on a spare coordinate give the requisite exclusion witnesses in d≥3. In d=2 the pivot has no singleton witness, the three-arm case is impossible, and the repeated-arm triple is shattered exactly when q≥4, as its empty trace needs an unused value outside three on one coordinate and two on the other. The pair condition is exactly distance ≤2 outside d=1 and (d,q)=(2,2); in the latter every ball misses only one vertex. Counting the three types and applying Pascal's identity gives the stated formula. Independent raw traces in branches/224c8b6a-87ed-4117-9045-0533e8f21052/verify_record4_raw.py reproduced all counts through support size four at (2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,2),(3,3),(4,2); this is finite corroboration.
